cita: Guo et al. (2026). EET: Experience-Driven Early Termination for Cost-Efficient Software Engineering Agents.
problema: SE agents resolve GitHub issues via multi-round LLM iterations whose conversation-history context grows super-linearly ('token snowball'), and agents often keep iterating on hopeless or already-solved issues, wasting substantial monetary/API cost without improving resolution rate.
mecanismo: EET distills each historical issue-resolution trajectory into a structured experience object (concise issue abstraction, compressed execution_summary, pass-only evaluation, plus a confidence/confidence_reason retrospective) retrieved via TF-IDF similarity above a threshold; at inference it augments patch generation with dual-milestone (code-modification, test-execution) confidence checks that trigger early termination, and independently scores each generated patch (confidence vs. two thresholds) to stop redundant patch-selection iterations early.
evaluacion: SWE-bench Verified (500 real GitHub issue tasks) across three SE agents (Agentless, Mini-SWE-Agent, Trae Agent) x two backbones (GPT-5-mini, DeepSeek-V3.2), compared against Turn-control and a Naive-EET (raw-trajectory RAG) baseline; experience mined from a deduplicated 207-task subset of SWE-bench Lite; RQ1-3 ablations isolate experience injection vs. early termination.
numeros_clave: Table 1/3: EET cuts total cost 19.3%-55.1% (avg 31.8%) with <=0.2% resolution-rate loss (even +2.7% avg gain), vs. -10.7% resolution rate for Turn-control at -41.4% cost; reduces API calls/input/output tokens by avg 20.8%/29.9%/25.1%; early-termination fires on avg 11.3% of issues (Table 2); confidence>90 patches show 63.6-92.6% pass rate vs 8.7-13.8% for confidence<40.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Table 1/3 directly measures per-issue cost/token/API-call reduction from experience-guided early termination (avg -31.8% total cost, negligible performance loss), a strong quantitative confirmation of MF's context/cost-economy thesis.
Experience objects are written only from successfully validated trajectories (evaluation_result=pass, SS3.1), an outcome-gated write trigger MF's G-M1 (discretionary write) could adopt directly.

EET stores one experience-object-per-issue in a single TF-IDF-indexed base retrieved by the issue description (SS3.1) -- a single-source-per-fact design relevant to MF's COSTURAS question, though not explicitly framed as a multi-store seam problem.

notes: Table 1 (RQ1 main cost/performance results), Table 2 (early-termination rate), Table 3 (RQ2 baseline comparison) anchor the numbers; confidence-calibration analysis in Appendix M grounds the reliability claim (SS5.1).

cita: Biswal et al. (2026). AgentSM: Semantic Memory for Agentic Text-to-SQL.
problema: Agentic Text-to-SQL systems on realistic enterprise schemas (Spider 2.0) repeat identical exploration steps across queries on the same database, rigidly apply one-size-fits-all strategies regardless of task, and exhibit high run-to-run variance -- inflating cost/latency and destabilizing accuracy at scale.
mecanismo: AgentSM builds a structured trajectory store: synthetic exploration questions are generated offline per schema and executed to produce dense exploration traces; trajectories are step-classified (exploration/execution/validation) and re-formatted as LLM-annotated Markdown with semantic headers; at inference the planner retrieves the single most-similar prior trajectory segment (same database, top-1 by question similarity) to skip redundant schema exploration, while frequently co-occurring tool pairs are fused into composite tools (e.g., get_ext+get_ddl -> local_exploration) to shorten trajectories.
evaluacion: Spider 2.0 / Spider 2.0 Lite benchmark (547 enterprise-scale multi-dialect Text-to-SQL tasks); ablation on a 20-question sample compares no-trajectory vs. naive raw-trajectory vs. structured Markdown/JSON trajectory formats, measuring average steps and execution accuracy.
numeros_clave: State-of-the-art 44.8% execution accuracy on Spider 2.0 Lite; reduces average token usage by 25% and trajectory length by 35% vs. SOTA; Table 1 ablation: raw/naive trajectories give NO improvement (22.62 steps/25% acc, same as no-trajectory) while structured Markdown trajectories cut steps to 16.50 and raise accuracy to 50% (JSON: 15.12 steps/50%).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Table 1 is a direct, measured demonstration that raw/unstructured trajectory dumps give ZERO benefit while typed, structured (Markdown/JSON) trajectory representations cut steps ~33% and lift accuracy 2x -- confirms MF's TIER-DOCS thesis that typed narrative beats raw log dumping as ground-truth memory.
Reported 25% token reduction and 35% trajectory-length reduction (abstract) via trajectory reuse and composite-tool fusion directly supports MF's context-economy framing.

Composite tools (SS3.3) mine consistently co-occurring tool pairs across historical trajectories and freeze them into a single reusable action, an automated consolidation-of-routine pattern MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor could adopt.

notes: Table 1 (SS3.2 trajectory-structure ablation) is the key mechanism-validating number; Fig.2 (repeated-exploration measurement on Spider 2's firebase DB) and Fig.4 (composite-tool mining) anchor the motivating opportunities in SS2.1.

cita: Mi et al. (2026). Darwinian Memory: A Training-Free Self-Regulating Memory System for GUI Agent Evolution.
problema: GUI agents on long-horizon, cross-app tasks suffer context amnesia from limited context windows, and existing memory paradigms either rigidly couple high-level intent to entire fixed low-level trajectories (breaking under dynamic layout changes) or statically accumulate outdated/toxic trajectories with no mechanism to purge them.
mecanismo: DMS decomposes trajectories into independent reusable (Precondition,Goal)-tagged sub-plan units with their dense action trajectory, retrieved via dual-factor (precondition x goal) cosine-similarity matching; a survival value S(mi) combines log-diminishing reuse utility, sigmoid temporal decay (with usage-extended half-life) and a Bayesian reliability penalty from verification failures, pruned via an Elbow-method cutoff on the ranked utility curve; an epsilon-mutation mechanism lets the agent re-attempt a sub-task from scratch and overwrite the stored trajectory in-place if the new one is shorter/more efficient, while a Beta-Binomial Bayesian risk score suppresses historically failure-prone plans.
evaluacion: AndroidWorld benchmark (116 tasks x 20 real apps, millions of parameterized variants) across four general-purpose MLLM backbones (Qwen2.5-VL-72B, Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B, GLM-4.5V, Seed1.6-VL) comparing PA-Lite baseline vs. DMS-PA-Lite, plus a 5-round memory-reuse-rate and success/stability(SRR)-over-rounds analysis.
numeros_clave: Table 1: DMS-PA-Lite reaches 66.4% success with Qwen2.5-VL-72B (+25.4pp over PA-Lite baseline), avg gains of +18.0% success rate and +33.9% execution stability across 4 backbones while reducing task latency (e.g. -4.75% for Qwen2.5-VL); memory reuse rate climbs from ~12% (round1) to >30% (round5), stabilizing at a 30-36% structural ceiling (Fig.4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The composite survival value explicitly penalizes 'toxic priors' via temporal decay + a Bayesian reliability penalty driven by post-execution verification failures (SS3.2.3), a concrete staleness/poisoning-mitigation mechanism relevant to MF's FIDELIDAD anchor.

epsilon-Mutation triggers in-place evolutionary overwrite of a stored trajectory only when a re-attempt proves shorter/more efficient (SS3.2.2), a concrete promotion-of-better-recipe mechanism MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor could draw from.

DMS reports consistent task-latency reductions alongside accuracy gains (Fig.1, abstract) by replaying verified sub-trajectories instead of re-generating them, confirming MF's context/latency-economy framing.

notes: Table 1 (main AndroidWorld results) and Fig.4 (memory-reuse-rate heatmap over 5 rounds) anchor the quantitative claims; SS3.2.3 formalizes the survival-value pruning law.

cita: Mi et al. (2026). Skill-Pro: Learning Reusable Skills from Experience via Non-Parametric PPO for LLM Agents.
problema: LLM agents re-derive solutions from scratch even in recurring situations because episodic-memory approaches merely retrieve past cases as 'history books' requiring inference-heavy re-reasoning at decision time, producing computational redundancy and unreliable long-horizon execution -- while parametric fine-tuning to fix this is costly and forgets.
mecanismo: Skill-Pro formalizes a Skill-MDP where procedural memory is a pool of explicit Skills omega=(activation-condition, execution-procedure, termination-condition); Non-Parametric PPO evolves the pool without weight updates via Semantic Gradients (per-trajectory hindsight-attribution feedback on each Skill component, batch-aggregated into a natural-language update direction that revises the Skill) filtered by a PPO-style trust-region Gate (a clipped importance-ratio/advantage verification functional under the frozen LLM policy admitting only candidates with positive expected advantage), plus online score-based pruning (advantage-per-invocation) that removes non-positive-score or duplicate Skills to keep the pool compact.
evaluacion: ALFWorld and TextArena benchmarks; in-domain, cross-task (out-of-distribution/higher-difficulty), and cross-agent (heterogeneous LLM backbones: Gemma-3-4B, Qwen3-32B, LLaMA-3.3-70B) reuse-rate and performance evaluation vs. RAG, ExpeL, A-MEM, AWM, G-Memory, ReAct, CoT baselines, plus ablations on Semantic Gradients / PPO Gate / online scoring.
numeros_clave: Table 1: Skill-Pro reuse rate 0.925 (in-domain)/0.825-0.90 (cross-task)/0.85-0.875 (cross-agent) vs best baseline RAG 0.349/0.44-0.47; storage cost 816 total stored tokens vs 40510-391706 for baselines (>50x compression); Table 2: ALFWorld success 0.90 (train)/0.909 (OOD) vs best baseline AWM 0.70/0.90.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Non-Parametric PPO's Semantic Gradient + PPO Gate (SS4.1-4.2) is a formalized, verifiable procedure for revising and admitting a refined Skill into the pool only if it passes a trust-region advantage test -- a rigorous consolidation/promotion gate MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor could adopt beyond ad hoc gotcha-to-recipe promotion.

Table 1 shows Skill-Pro's procedural memory footprint (816 total stored tokens) is 50-500x smaller than episodic/insight/workflow baselines (40510-391706 tokens) while achieving higher reuse and task success (Table 2) -- a strong confirmation of MF's context-economy thesis that typed procedural memory beats raw episodic accumulation.

The Skill pool acts as a small, evolvable derived index over raw interaction trajectories (SS3.4-4.3) rather than the ground truth itself, echoing MF's Tier-3 derived-index framing, though the paper doesn't discuss staleness/rebuild relative to a Tier-1 source.

notes: Table 1 (SS5.2, reuse rate + storage/execution cost) and Table 2 (task performance) anchor the quantitative claims; Fig.2 diagrams the Skill-MDP + Non-Parametric PPO pipeline (SS4).

cita: Zhang et al. (2026). TextBFGS: A Case-Based Reasoning Approach to Code Optimization via Error-Operator Retrieval.
problema: LLM self-correction/code-optimization methods (TextGrad-style textual gradient descent) are stateless first-order optimizers: each run starts from scratch, ignoring past debugging experience and the 'semantic curvature' of the error landscape, causing inefficient zig-zagging and excessive token consumption to converge.
mecanismo: TextBFGS maintains a Hessian-Proxy Case Base of (gradient, operator) tuples -- historical error/feedback descriptions paired with the abstract correction operator that resolved them -- and retrieves top-k operators by error-similarity (not surface problem-similarity, unlike REMO) using the previous step's gradient as a 'semantic momentum' query; a single LLM call (One-Pass Update) simultaneously diagnoses the current error (<GRADIENT>), generates/reuses a correction operator (<OPERATOR>) and revises the code (<IMPROVED>); successful updates are retained back into the Case Base (Retain), forming a self-evolving Retrieve-Reuse-Revise-Retain CBR loop.
evaluacion: HumanEval-Hard (45 tasks) and MBPP-Hard (117 tasks) filtered subsets from EvalPlus where the base model (Qwen3-235B-A22B) initially scores 0 on Pass@1; compared against TextGrad, TextGrad-Momentum, a no-Case-Base ablation (TextBFGS w/o CB), and TextBFGS-REMO (problem-similarity retrieval reproduction), including a cross-domain vs. in-domain Case-Base-source transfer experiment.
numeros_clave: On MBPP-Hard, Case Base integration lifts Plus pass rate from 58.12% (Momentum) to 78.63% (+20.51pp, Table 2); cross-domain transfer: TextBFGS (error-based retrieval) holds 74.36% Plus pass using a HumanEval-sourced case base to solve MBPP, vs. TextBFGS-REMO (problem-based retrieval) collapsing to 58.12% on the same cross-domain transfer (+16.24pp gap, Table 3 vs 4); One-Pass update reduces computational cost by ~50% vs standard multi-step methods (SS3.4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: TextBFGS deliberately indexes cases by error/gradient (not by surface problem text) as the single retrieval key (SS3.3, Eq.6), and this key choice is shown empirically to determine cross-domain transfer (Table 3 vs 4) -- a concrete lesson for MF's COSTURAS question of what the single source-of-truth key for a fact/lesson should be.

Table 2's ablation (Case Base integration: +20.51pp Plus pass rate on MBPP-Hard vs. Momentum-only) empirically confirms that retaining and reusing successful correction operators (a consolidation loop, SS3.5 Retain) materially improves outcomes over transient/no memory -- supports MF's CONSOLIDACION thesis.
SS3.4 reports the One-Pass fused diagnosis+operator+revision step cuts computational cost ~50% vs standard multi-step correction pipelines, confirming MF's context/latency-economy framing.

notes: Table 1/2 (HumanEval-Hard/MBPP-Hard ablations) and Table 3/4 (cross-domain vs in-domain retrieval) anchor the numbers; Fig.2 visualizes the TextGrad vs TextBFGS optimization-trajectory difference (SS3.2).

cita: Mokssit, Ravi, Nie, Kim & Liu (2026). FHIR-AgentEval: A Modular Sandbox for Benchmarking Clinical LLM Agents with an Evaluation of Memory-Augmented Configurations.
problema: LLM agents translating natural-language clinical requests into structured FHIR API operations are unreliable for realistic appointment-management/genetic-testing workflows (prior work shows a steep drop from read-only Q&A to multi-step write/action tasks), with strategic failures like incorrect tool selection and resource-type confusion, and no rigorous sandboxed benchmark existed to measure whether memory helps.
mecanismo: FHIR-AgentEval provides 43 modular tasks against a resettable HAPI FHIR R4 server with deterministic + soft (LLM-judge) validators; agents (LangChain ReAct/GPT-4.1-mini, capped 15 iterations) are evaluated in 5 configurations varying access to an on-demand FHIR-specs MCP server and a Reflexion-inspired long-term-memory MCP server, whose micro (per resource/operation tip) and macro (task-level strategic) reflections are distilled offline by a GPT-4.1 evaluator + o4-mini reflector from training-task trajectories and indexed in a dual FAISS store (semantic for macro, structured-metadata exact-match for micro).
evaluacion: Four experimental settings (seen variations; unseen variations; paraphrased prompts; held-out tasks) across five agent configurations (baseline, +specs, +memory no-specs-training, +memory specs-trained, +memory specs-trained+specs), measuring task success rate (mean +/- SD over 3 runs), variance decomposition (same-prompt/within-task/between-task), failure-mode flags, tool-call counts and token usage.
numeros_clave: Best memory configuration (Memory specs-trained+FHIR specs) beats baseline by +22.5% (Exp.1) and +27.9% (Exp.2); on held-out tasks (Exp.4) best memory config (no-specs-training) reaches 60.6% overall success, +9.1% over baseline (abstract); memory-enhanced configs show lower total variance (2503-2643 vs 2879-2905 squared pp for baselines) driven by reduced between-task variance (42-49% vs >54%).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The ablation across 5 configurations isolates that memory (not raw spec access alone) is what reduces strategic failures like incorrect tool selection/resource-type confusion (Discussion, Fig.7-8) -- a measured demonstration that retrieval mechanism/content matters more than mere context availability, aligning with MF's G-M2 measured-retrieval stance.

Reflexion training distills micro (operation-level tips) vs. macro (task-level strategic) reflections from execution logs offline (SS Reflexion training process), a two-granularity consolidation scheme MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor could adopt for promoting gotchas at different scopes.

Memory-augmented configurations consistently show HIGHER median token usage than baseline (Fig.10) despite better success/stability -- relevant context for MF's context-economy tradeoff (accuracy vs. token cost), without a clear net-favorable verdict either way.

notes: Held-out-task results (Exp.4, Discussion) and variance-decomposition analysis (Fig.6) anchor the quantitative claims; failure-mode taxonomy (Fig.7-8: incorrect tool selection/order, resource-type confusion) grounds the qualitative mechanism claims.
